title: [observability] Every alert ends with an outcome, the owner can judge a wrong one, and the Core lines card says how often Needs you was right
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_alerts`, `spawn_alert_record`, the control fold's `alert.fired` and `alert.cleared`), crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs (`ALERTS`, the rows /api/alerts gives), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (`command`, the `spawn alerts` verb) and main.rs, and serve.rs's core-lines module (objective 084; 088's observability line if it is in).

This comes after objectives 084 (the Core lines frame) and 089 (the guardrail alert, which the acceptance uses for a running loop). Both must be in the tree.

The problem (owner, 2026-11-12 13:30; sync/roadmap-effects.md, Observability, north star "Needs you is right"). The observability line's north star is the share of the items Needs you showed in the last 7 days that were true and really needed the owner. The record cannot tell. An alert is open or cleared, and a cleared one looks the same whether its condition went away (it was right) or it was false, stale or a duplicate of another (it was wrong). By hand on 11-12 there were four false "message not taken" alerts in one day, and nothing on the page counted them.

Required behaviour.
(a) `spawn alert judge <key> false|stale|duplicate` is the owner's verb.
- It records `alert.judged` {key, verdict} through spawn_alert_record (owner only) and prints what it judged.
- An open alert it judges is cleared by it, with cleared evidence {judged: <verdict>}. A cleared alert keeps its cleared evidence and gains the verdict.
- It refuses, exiting other than 0 and writing nothing: another verdict, a key no alert has, a notice, and an alert already judged.
- The fold keeps the verdict and its time on the alert's row, and a refold gives the same rows.
- Only the owner judges: the verb goes through spawn_alert_record, which refuses any other login (spawn_mission_caller), so no agent can judge an alert.
- A running loop learns of the judgement. The alert step today loads the alerts it knows only at its start (Monitor::start). After the owner judges an open alert, the loop's next pass must treat it as cleared: refresh what it knows each pass, or take a refused clear of an alert that is no longer open as cleared. So it never retries a clear the store refuses, and a later real occurrence of the same kind and subject fires as usual (089's guardrail alert among them), with no restart needed.
(b) `GET /api/alerts`' rows carry `outcome`: null while open (and for a notice), "cleared" when its condition cleared it, else its verdict.
(c) `GET /api/core-lines`' north star `observability.needs_you_right`: of the alerts (not notices) that ended in the last 7 days (cleared_at_ms within them), the share whose outcome is "cleared". It is null with none. It counts alerts only; the supervisor's questions and escalations in Needs you are not in it (yet). Ranges and states are as for every figure (084).
(d) The page lets the owner judge an alert from Needs you, or names the verb beside it. Read off a screenshot.
No gate, integrator or deploy step reads the outcomes or the figure.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/092.sh, on 089's world: a real `spawn loop` and `spawn serve`, guardrails raised and cleared after 2 s. Alerts are seeded as the loop records them (spawn_alert_record): a1 and a2 fired and cleared, a3 and a4 fired and open, a5 a notice. Checks (1) to (3) run before the loop starts:
- (1) `spawn alert judge bb:a2 false` and `bb:a3 duplicate` succeed, and two alert.judged are recorded. "bb:a1 wrong", "bb:none false", "bb:a2 stale" (judged already) and "bb:a5 false" (a notice) are refused and write nothing.
- (2) Through `GET /api/alerts`:
  - the outcomes are a1 cleared, a2 false, a3 duplicate (and cleared, its cleared evidence {judged: duplicate}), a4 null (open) and a5 null (notice);
  - a2 keeps the evidence it was cleared with.
- (3) Through `GET /api/core-lines`: needs_you_right is 1/3 (a1 right of a1, a2 and a3 ended), with no range set.
- (4) Then the loop runs with free disk out of its range, and its guardrail alert opens. The owner judges it false. Free disk goes back in range for 8 s, then out again. Within 60 s a new alert for the same subject opens, the judged one stays cleared and false, and the loop's log shows no retried clear of it. A loop that keeps the judged alert open in memory fails both (proved on a throwaway without the refresh: sync/obj-092/f1-mutant-no-refresh.log).
It fails with 1 on f41cbcc1: there is no `spawn alert` verb, no outcome, and no /api/core-lines. Its throwaway stacks the throwaways of 084 and 089 (sync/obj-092/throwaway-f1.diff).

Once this lands: 088's "not measured" falls by one. The roadmap's range for the north star is "9 in 10 or more"; the lead sets it once a week of outcomes exists.

The product reason. Needs you is only worth reading if it is right, and the owner is the one who knows when it was not. One verb records that, and the figure turns "a few false alerts today" into a number the observability line steers by. Monitoring only.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (045, 057, 074 and 084 among them) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour:
- a spawn-postgres test of alert.judged through the real store (open, cleared, a notice refused, judged twice refused, a refold);
- a CLI test of the verb's usage;
- an alert-step unit test: an open alert judged while the loop runs is cleared in the loop's view by its next pass, no refused clear is retried, and a new occurrence of the same kind and subject fires;
- a core-lines unit test of the share (none ended, a notice left out, outside the window).
